title: personal-reading-summaries-scratchpad
content:
Fast scratchpad for papers/blogs/conference takeaways — messy, intentionally so. Goal: capture things I want to try in infra serving/runtime experiments and prompts for later write-ups.

1) Papers & quicknotes (sketchy)
- FlashAttention (2022): short summary: algorithm + cuda kernels to reduce memory and memory-bandwidth for attention via tiling and fused kernels. Practical for inference: huge win for long sequences, reduces peak memory and exposes compute patterns good for kernel fusion.
  - Takeaway: benchmark our runtime with FlashAttention-enabled kernels for 8k/16k sequences. See if throughput per-GPU improves vs current kernels when kv-cache is heavy.
  - TODO: add a small microbenchmark (causal transformer, batch sizes [1,4,16], seqLens [512,2048,8192]) next sprint.

- QLoRA / 4-bit quant finetuning notes: cheap fine-tuning with quantized weights; mostly relevant for smaller specialized models and on-device. Not directly applicable for large multi-tenant hosted models but useful for private deployments where customers bring small proprietary datasets.
  - Question: could we provide a managed QLoRA pipeline as part of Private offering? Ops concerns: reproducibility, checkpoint storage, KMS for data at rest.

- "Efficient Transformer Inference Survey" (internal reading notes): key levers collated: kernel fusion, flash-attn, rotary vs absolute pos embeddings, KV-cache sparsity, prefix caching, activation quantization.
  - Prioritize: kernel fusion + dynamic batching policy + prefix caching heuristics.

2) Blog posts / product posts I liked
- Llama 3 announcement / blog: model variants + safety guardrails. Thought: when we expose model catalog, show curated model profiles (safety, latency, cost) + recommended use-cases.
- Engineering blog on productionizing LLMs (unknown author): interesting operational patterns — shadow traffic experiments, progressive rollout windows, and automatic fallback to smaller model family on overload. Matches Redwood's routing ideas.

3) Conference takeaways (AIConf 2025 workshop notes)
- Talk: "Latency SLOs at scale" — speaker emphasized multi-tier routing: hot-path low-latency models reserved for SLAs; best-effort pool for burst. Also highlighted value of coarse-grained autoscaling triggers (queue-length percentiles) vs token-level heuristics.
  - Action: examine current autoscaler triggers in dedicated clusters. Add queue-length percentile metric to SRE dashboard.

- Panel: "Quality-aware routing" — use small proxy-model to predict output quality when routing to quantized/accelerated variants. Very interesting: cheap-to-evaluate classifier to decide when to route to high-accuracy variant.
  - Idea: Implement a lightweight predictor (distilled) that takes prompt features + sample output and decides whether to re-run on higher-fidelity model. Prototype path: create two-model pipeline in dev env and measure cost delta vs quality bump.

4) Short experiments to try (concrete)
- Experiment A: FlashAttn kernel toggle. Run 3 jobs: (1) baseline kernel, (2) flash-attn fused kernel, (3) fused + activation quant. Metrics: p99 latency, tokens/sec, memory peak, cost per 1M tokens. Deliverable: one-pager with benchmark tables and recommendation.

- Experiment B: Prefix caching policy. Implement heuristic: if request has prefix hash seen > N times in last T minutes, hit in-memory prefix cache; else regular path. Measure cache hit rate and tail-latency improvement.

- Experiment C: Quality predictor for routing. Collect dataset: prompts labeled pass/fail on acceptance criteria. Train small encoder-only model (tiny) to predict probability that quantized model output will pass. Evaluate ROC and false-negative cost.

5) Implementation notes / things to watch
- Kernel switching: need to ensure deterministic outputs if customers pin versions. Kernel selection should be a runtime build flag, not silently change outputs for pinned model versions. Add metadata on model-versions: kernels recommended + signed checksum for deterministic serving.
- Logging: sample outputs for any reroute decisions, attach reason codes (e.g., "quality-predictor-failed" or "resource-fallback"), but keep samples small to limit exfil risk.
- Metrics: define cost-per-query and quality-per-query. Need long-running experiment pipeline to compute rolling averages and detect regressions after kernel changes.

6) Open questions / follow-ups
- How to reconcile quantized-faster variants with reproducibility? If we serve quantized variants as default for cost reasons, we must surface the delta in expected outputs to customers. Should be opt-in or visible in model metadata.
- Can we get FlashAttention authors to sanity-check our kernel integration? Maybe reach out or open a GitHub issue with minimal repro.

7) Notes-to-self (short checklist)
- [ ] Create microbenchmark harness in serving-runtime repo (issue: serv-runtime#TODO).
- [ ] Add queue-length percentile to dedicated cluster autoscaling dashboard.
- [ ] Prototype quality predictor pipeline using ~5k prompt/label pairs.
- [ ] Draft 1-pager for product: "When to recommend quantized model variants" for Private customers.

8) Random scribbles / fragments worth keeping
- "If we can reduce p99 by 30% for long-context workloads, we unlock new class of multimodal customers."
- Note: check memory fragmentation on long-lived processes (NVidia caching allocator) — might explain degraded perf over 24h runs.

End of scratchpad. Keep this file lightweight and mutable. Will extract a polished doc when experiments complete.

Last edited: quick note appended 2026-03-05: prioritize FlashAttention microbench + prefix cache prototype. Reassign Maya for data collection.
